newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dutch PM says chance of EMU postponement "minimal".
newsitem.headline: Dutch PM says chance of EMU postponement "minimal".

text.p: Dutch Prime Minister Wim Kok said on Friday the chances of European economic and monetary union (EMU) being postponed were minimal.
"We will continue to do everything possible to avoid postponement," he told a news conference after the regular weekly meeting of the Dutch cabinet.
Asked by reporters how great he thought the chance was that monetary union might be postponed, Kok replied: "Minimal."
EMU's third phase, the launch of a single European Currency known as the euro, is scheduled for January 1, 1999.
But fresh doubts emerged this week that Germany -- widely seen as the anchor nation for economic and monetary union -- could meet the budgetary target required to qualify for EMU.
Kok said there were no differences between himself and Dutch Foreign Minister Hans van Mierlo about the unlikelihood and undesirability of a delayed launch for the single currency.
"I would regard postponement as grave, just like the minister of foreign affairs," he said.
Van Mierlo told Dutch television on Thursday that any postoponement of EMU would be damaging for the process of integration within the European Union.

"If you had to postpone EMU, then there is a chance that the prospect of getting it would become diluted and that could lead to signs of disintegration...we could indeed go backwards in the process of coming closer together," he said.
The Netherlands holds the European Union presidency in the first half of 1997 and hopes to draft a treaty on EU reform in time for it to be signed at a June summit in Amsterdam.
